Desk rules for supply orders
Everyone on the desk should know how the desk handles it

Supply handling and travel checks

This section keeps the Companion Animal Travel Desk moving cleanly and keeps animal care from slipping during rush work. Every order, handoff, and record note must stay clear, current, and easy to trace.

Use only approved forms for supply requests, carrier checks, comfort items, and hazard notes. If a traveler arrives with a pet that needs extra space, water, padding, or a calmer route, record it at once and pass it to the welfare coordinator without delay. Safety comes first, so do not release an animal for movement until the safety coordinator has cleared the setup and the comfort review is noted. <<FACT F106>> After that, keep the file open and watch for changes in the traveler plan, crate condition, or pet behavior.

All boarding records must be complete before the animal is moved forward. <<FACT F093>> If any detail is missing, stop the handoff and call for correction right away. The desk should not guess, backfill, or leave a note half-finished. Use plain language, keep names matched to the right booking, and make sure the carrier tag, pet notes, and owner contact details agree with the record. If a traveler like Caleb Cohen, Mariam Mendes, or a pet like Cali is on the file, keep the same careful standard and check each line again before release.

If a problem lands on the desk and the next step is not obvious, contact the senior coordinator at once.
